text:
Pranav: quick one — we've had two customer reports where requests with both X-Workspace and X-VPC-Endpoint headers landed on the shared dedicated pool instead of the customer's private pool. I thought VPC/private endpoint should win. Anyone changed precedence lately?
Sam: hmm not intentionally. can you paste the raw headers & example request id?
Pranav: sure — repro: header X-Workspace: ws-acme, X-VPC-Endpoint: vpce-1234, route matched: dedicated-shared-pool-1, trace id 01-abc. Happened ~10:12 PDT.
Maria: that shouldn't be happening in strict mode. Our ruleset order is supposed to prefer explicit pool affinity (vpc/pool) over workspace fallbacks. Maybe the gateway evaluated header scrubbing earlier?
Kevin: we added a small optimization to short-circuit route matching for token-based routing last week. if token->workspace mapping exists, it sometimes bails before header checks. might be the culprit.
Alyssa: customers expect private endpoints to be non-bypassable. If a VPC endpoint is provided we should never route to shared pools unless capacity fallback is explicitly allowed. needs product confirmation but UX should be clear.
Sam: agreed. we have two behaviours in code now: 
```yaml
- match: header(X-VPC-Endpoint)
  action: route_to_private_pool
  precedence: 200
- match: token_workspace(TOKEN)
  action: route_to_workspace_pool
  precedence: 100
# but fast-path token routing can skip header checks in hot path
```
Sam: the fast-path was to cut tail latency, but it violated strict-scoped routing.
Pranav: this explains the reports. can we make header checks authoritative for VPC/Private endpoint?
Kevin: quick fix: add a preflight check that if X-VPC-Endpoint present -> force evaluation of vpc rules first. minimal perf impact. longer term we should unify matching into a single deterministic priority table.
Maria: also add a telemetry tag when we do the fast-path skip: routing.decision=skipped_header_check so we can find regressions.
ops-bot: [test-runner] smoke tests: added case vpce + workspace -> expecting private-pool, current behavior 8/10 correct, 2/10 hit shared due to fast-path. full logs: link: https://ci/internal/1850012345/logs
Alyssa: for console UX we should expose an explicit "routing precedence" toggle per workspace (Strict VPC precedence vs Workspace-first). default to Strict VPC for private endpoints.
Pranav: +1. and also make the rollout opt-in (feature flag) for a small % of requests while we monitor.
Sam: plan: 1) revert token fast-path for routing selection (or gate behind feature flag), 2) add preflight header authoritative rule for X-VPC-Endpoint, 3) emit telemetry keys: routing.decision, routing.reason, routing.fallback_count, routing.target_pool.
Kevin: I'll draft the minimal code change. sample preflight pseudocode: 
```js
if (req.headers['x-vpc-endpoint']) {
  route = matchVpcEndpoint(req) || fallbackToWorkspace(req)
} else {
  route = tokenFastPath(req) || fullMatch(req)
}
```
Kevin: add metric when fallbackToWorkspace is used: routing.fallback.reason=capacity|no_pool|policy.
Alyssa: product asks that fallback must emit an alert when it affects SLA-bound customers. add severity label in telemetry.
Maria: good call. also add an admin console view: per-workspace route decisions (last 24h) + % fallbacks. ops wants links to traces.
deploy-bot: starting canary rollout for 'vpc-strict-precedence' flag -> 5% traffic now.
Pranav: i'll monitor traces and customer tickets. if we see anything weird we'll pause. thanks all.
Sam: I'll open a PR with the revert + preflight change and link the canary dashboard.
Kevin: PR up in ~30m. tagging @Maria for telemetry dashboard additions.
Maria: noted. will add dashboard panels: routing.decision counts, fallback latencies, and per-workspace fallback heatmap.
Pranav: closing loop — will file follow-up to update docs & API contract so Engineering + Support know VPC header is authoritative.
Alyssa: also notify CSMs for customers with private endpoints to expect the change in routing semantics (will reduce cross-tenant routing).
Pranav: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
